extracted.intended_audience: researchers and conference organizers studying peer review and the effects of LLM assistance (machine learning research community)
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and measurement framework for how LLM-assisted papers and LLM-assisted reviews interact in conference peer review; includes detection, causal/regression identification, within-paper paired analyses, synthetic LLM review generation, and metrics for review influence and alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM detection (α mixture estimation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the statistical method from Liang et al. which models LLM-generated and human text as distinct distributions and estimates the fraction α of LLM-generated text via maximum likelihood estimation (treating text as drawn from a weighted mixture of LLM and Human token distributions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: α depends on a bag-of-words token probability model; reference LLM distribution is based on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o outputs. Advantages: ease of use, fast inference, robustness to partially LLM-aided text. Limitations: may underestimate use of other models (e.g., Claude, Gemini) and depends on reference distribution choice. See Appendix A.3 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification as LLM-aided (α threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify documents (papers or reviews) as LLM-aided if α > α_threshold where α_threshold = 0.15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This binary classification is used throughout analyses (e.g., to form quadrants of (Paper, Review) LLM status). Choice of threshold affects counts and sensitivity; authors note using α_threshold = 0.15 to mark 'substantial LLM modification.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Review score components (presentation, contribution, soundness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews include auxiliary numeric scores for Presentation, Contribution, and Soundness (each scored 1–4 in ICLR reviewer template).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fields are analyzed alongside the overall rating to study where LLM-aided reviews differ (e.g., presentation or soundness). The synthetic review prompts request these exact fields in JSON to enable direct comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall rating and conference-specific rating scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall rating is the principal outcome variable; ICLR uses the mapping {1: Strong Reject, 3: Reject, 5: Marginally below acceptance, 6: Marginally above acceptance, 8: Accept, 10: Strong accept}. Other conferences use similar numerical scales (NeurIPS 1–6, ICML 1–5 as used in generation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall rating is used in regressions, within-paper differences, and alignment calculations. Synthetic LLM reviews are generated to output ratings consistent with each conference's official scale (prompts embed the conference rating scale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (reviewer certainty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide a Confidence score indicating certainty about their assessment (ICLR confidence scale described from 1 to 5 where 1 = not confident, 5 = absolutely certain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidence is used as an auxiliary metric (e.g., comparing confidence for LLM-aided vs. human reviews). Synthetic reviews are asked to supply a confidence score per the conference scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of treatment and paper LLM status (causal variables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define treatment T_{ij} ∈ {0,1} as whether review slot j for paper i was assigned to a reviewer that used LLM assistance; define X_i^{LLM} ∈ {0,1} as whether paper i contains LLM-assisted text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These variables are the core inputs to the causal model and regression (Eq. 2) and to within-paper paired analyses; precise definitions matter for identification and interpretation of effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression causal model and interpretation of coefficients (β0, β1, β2, β3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model rating Y_{ij} = β0 + β1 X_i^{LLM} + β2 T_{ij} + β3 (X_i^{LLM} × T_{ij}) + γ' Z_i + ε_{ij}. β0 is baseline (human paper, human review); β1 difference for LLM-assisted papers; β2 is CATE of LLM-aided review on human papers; β2+β3 is CATE on LLM papers; β3 is the interaction capturing relative leniency of LLM reviews to LLM-assisted papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include area fixed effects in Z_i to control for confounding by subject area. β3 is the primary quantity of interest for detecting differential kindness. Report estimates with 95% CI and p-values; be cautious of unobserved confounding, multicollinearity, and collider bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key identification assumption: conditional ignorability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T_{ij} ⟂ {Y_{ij}(0), Y_{ij}(1)} | X_i (treatment assignment independent of potential outcomes conditional on observed paper covariates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors condition on paper area and paper LLM status; discuss limitations (unobserved paper-level characteristics may still bias estimates) and motivate within-paper paired analysis as a more stringent identification strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: SUTVA and interference considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for potential violations of SUTVA because OpenReview allows post-rebuttal edits and reviewer discussions; authors note (1) most reviews (75–81%) remain unchanged and (2) co-reviewer influence tends to push reviews toward consensus, which they argue would likely dampen amplification of differential effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that access only to final post-rebuttal ratings limits claims; check sensitivity to pre/post-rebuttal interference where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Within-paper paired analysis (Δ_i)
rubrics_metrics.description: For papers that received at least one human review and at least one LLM-assisted review, compute per-paper treatment effect Δ_i = ar{Y}_i^{LLM} - ar{Y}_i^{Human}; estimate CATEs by averaging Δ_i over LLM vs human papers and test distributional differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This controls for between-paper confounding by holding paper fixed. Restricting to such papers introduces selection bias; use Mann-Whitney U test (one-tailed) to compare Δ_i distributions between paper types and report p-values and effect sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold-out human review as quality indicator and quality buckets
rubrics_metrics.description: Stratify papers by quality using a randomly selected hold-out human review as the quality indicator and create quality buckets (e.g., rating ≤3, =5, =6, ≥8 for ICLR) to analyze how LLM-review kindness varies with paper quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude the hold-out review when computing other metrics for that paper. Use bucket-specific regressions and within-paper analyses to reveal quality-dependent patterns (e.g., LLM-aided reviews inflate low-quality papers most).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review alignment with final decision (measure of review influence)
rubrics_metrics.description: A review 'aligns' with the final decision if its rating > 5 for accepted papers and ≤ 5 for rejected papers (ICLR threshold used here). Alignment rate = fraction of reviews aligning with outcome; compare alignment between human and LLM-aided reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a proxy for influence in final decisions; stratify alignment by paper quality buckets to examine whether LLM-aided reviews have different alignment in borderline cases. Report misalignment breakdowns (e.g., percent of LLM misalignments due to recommended acceptance for ultimately rejected papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrant summary statistics for (Paper, Review) LLM status
rubrics_metrics.description: Partition (paper, review) pairs into four quadrants (Human paper, Human review), (Human paper, LLM review), (LLM paper, Human review), (LLM paper, LLM review) and report mean ± std dev for Rating, Confidence, Presentation, Contribution, Soundness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These descriptive stats reveal initial patterns (e.g., LLM-assisted papers receive lower ratings on average; LLM-assisted reviews concentrate toward intermediate ratings) but can be confounded, motivating causal analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical testing framework (Mann-Whitney U, regressions with CIs and p-values)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Mann-Whitney U tests (one-tailed) to compare distributions of within-paper Δ_i and other nonparametric comparisons; use linear regressions with area fixed effects, report coefficient estimates, 95% confidence intervals, t-stats, and p-values to assess significance of effects (β coefficients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret effect sizes (e.g., small, very small, large) alongside p-values; run regressions within quality buckets to probe heterogeneity. Be careful about multiple testing and selection biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthetic fully LLM-generated review generation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate fully LLM reviews by prompting GPT-4o (avoid GPT-5) using conference-specific reviewer guidelines and a JSON review template; prompts request specific fields (e.g., Summary, Strengths, Weaknesses, Questions, Flag for ethics review, Presentation/Contribution/Soundness scores, Rating, Confidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompts are one-shot, include reviewer guidelines from conference websites, and explicitly require the JSON format. Sampling strategy: oversample LLM-aided papers to ensure sufficient power; generate reviews for randomly sampled papers from 2025 editions. Do not add instructions to be lenient/harsh to avoid biasing synthetic outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of rating compression and discriminative failure in fully LLM-generated reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether fully LLM-generated reviews exhibit rating compression (narrow distribution, e.g., almost exclusively between 6 and 7) and fail to discriminate paper quality (minimal slope across quality buckets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare synthetic LLM ratings to human ratings across quality buckets; compression implies inflated ratings for weak papers and poor signal for merit. Human-in-the-loop moderation can partially mitigate compression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metareview generation protocol and decision output format
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt area-chair simulator LLM to make final accept/reject decisions based on provided reviews and output exactly one JSON field: "decision": 1 (Accept) or 0 (Reject).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure whether LLM-assisted metareviews are more likely to render accept decisions than human metareviews given equivalent reviewer scores. Note: fully LLM-generated metareviews tended to be harsher in observational findings, while LLM-assisted metareviews were more likely to accept given equal scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of area fixed effects and control covariates
rubrics_metrics.description: Control for paper area via indicator variables (Z_i) in regressions to address confounding because certain subject areas may have both higher LLM adoption and different baseline rating distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area fixed effects are necessary to reduce bias from area-level confounding; report significant area coefficients where relevant. Beware of residual unobserved confounding and potential collider bias when adding many controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling and dataset inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses conducted on OpenReview data for ICLR (2024, 2025), NeurIPS (2024, 2025), ICML (2025); double-blind peer review conferences; collect full paper and review text, ratings, and paper metadata. Note ICLR keeps public pages for all papers; NeurIPS and ICML publicly keep mostly accepted papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset composition affects representativeness (e.g., overrepresentation of accepted papers for NeurIPS/ICML). Report counts (e.g., ~6.5k papers and 25k reviews per conference on average) and be transparent about public availability biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of β3 as differential kindness and caution about confounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret interaction coefficient β3 as the additional benefit of switching to an LLM-assisted reviewer for LLM-assisted papers relative to human papers; a positive β3 implies positive differential kindness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors emphasize that regression β3 can be affected by between-paper heterogeneity (e.g., LLM-assisted papers overrepresented in low-quality buckets) and that within-paper analyses reduce but may not fully eliminate biases. Report both regression and within-paper estimates for robustness.
